samples.summary: Large unrequested scope: a whole design-editor build-lane restructuring rides along with a frontend font-subsetting issue. The issue's area is `frontend`, it declares "Architecture change? No", and none of its acceptance criteria mention the lane graph, `packages/design-editor`, or #966. Yet the diff splits out a new `design-editor:build` lane, rewires `needs` on `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check` and `verify:entropy`, edits `harness.config.json`'s inert-path reason, rewrites `scripts/design.mjs`'s staleness check, adds build-if-stale logic to three `verify-*.mjs` scripts, and updates two design docs (`design-editor-packaging.md`, `harness-engineering.md`) — none of which affects font previews. Only the `verify:fast` addition of `design-editor build` is plausibly needed for the issue's "pnpm verify:fast passes" criterion; the rest is #966 follow-up that belongs in its own PR, where its risk (lane-graph selection) can be reviewed on its own terms.

The #966 stale-artefact fix is applied inconsistently: `verify-frame.mjs` still rebuilds only the shell. It boots `fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts` (line 46 + 122), which imports `@wafflebase/design-editor` BY NAME — the same path the diff argues (in verify-consumer.mjs, verify-scenes.mjs, verify-tokens.mjs) now resolves to `dist/plugin/index.js`. `buildShellIfStale` (lines 82–91) still runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` and `newestSourceMtime` (line 106) still ignores `tsconfig.build.json`, so this gate keeps exactly the trap the PR says cost an hour: a clean checkout dies with "dev server exited early", a dirty one paints against stale plugin bytes. If the design-editor half is in scope at all, this fourth consumer should have been updated with the others.

The build-if-stale helper is now copy-pasted a third and fourth time (verify-consumer.mjs `buildIfStale`, verify-scenes.mjs `buildDesignEditorIfStale`, verify-tokens.mjs `buildDesignEditorIfStale`, plus the pre-existing verify-frame.mjs and scripts/design.mjs versions) — identical `walk`, identical config list, identical artefact list, identical staleness rule. There is no shared script helper (no `scripts/lib/`), and the divergence it invites already shows: verify-frame.mjs was left behind and design.mjs uses a different artefact-vs-src comparison. One exported helper (e.g. under `scripts/`) consumed by all callers would match this repo's stated reuse preference.

The recents weight-resolution path partly works against the issue's own goal. Opening the dropdown now triggers `loadFullFontCatalog()` — the ~1,900-entry library module — whenever any recent family is missing from the curated catalog, purely to read a `weights` string, and holds those rows unpreviewable until it settles. The issue asks for cheaper preview loading and says the subset/weight should be "derived from what the row actually renders, not from a curated-catalog lookup that may miss"; a per-family fallback (e.g. omitting `:wght@` so css2 serves the family's default cut, or requesting the family's default weights on a miss) would satisfy that criterion without pulling a large JS payload on dropdown open and without the extra `fullSettled` state machine and observer deps this adds.

Preview requests exactly one cut, which is a small deviation from the issue's "Font rendering is unchanged — every previewed row … looks exactly as it does today". Rows are not all rendered at the first cut: `MoreFontsDialog` gives the selected row `font-medium` (500) and the previous full link carried `400;700`, so a selected row that used to have a real heavier cut now gets a synthesised one. Low visual impact given the shipped catalogs all list 400 first, but it is a rendering change the issue said would not happen.

The doc replaces the auditable figure "selects 6 of 28 lanes" with "selects a handful of lanes". The surrounding section's value is that the counts are checkable against the lane graph; softening it to "a handful" loses that. Since the diff knows the new count (the new build lane is one more), state it.

verdict.reason: The code exists, but the finding's premise — that the lane-graph work is unrequested #966 follow-up that "does not affect" this issue — is concretely contradicted. `verify:entropy` is `anyPkg: true` (scripts/verify-self.mjs:441-465) and the pinned invariant in scripts/test/verify-self-lanes.test.mjs:185-186 is that it runs on ANY package change, i.e. on this frontend-only font PR. Since packages/design-editor/package.json:6-10 resolves `exports["."]` to `dist/plugin/index.js`, and knip loads packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:49 which imports the package by name (knip.json:33,43), an unbuilt checkout makes verify-entropy.mjs:307-324 report `Could not parse knip output as JSON`. So the `design-editor:build` lane plus the `needs` edges on design-editor:check / design-sandbox:check / verify:entropy are prerequisites for this PR's own CI, not detachable scope. They are also the only shape allowed by the graph's own pinned invariant that a build folded into a sibling lane's `cmd` cannot be a `needs` edge (verify-self.mjs:338-347; verify-self-lanes.test.mjs:94-126). No stated Non-Goal is exceeded: the issue's "Out of scope" (docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md:58-62) covers only ensureFontLink/findFontLink and `?subset=menu`, while its acceptance "pnpm verify:fast green" (line 56) maps onto package.json:14, which runs design-editor build and design-sandbox typecheck/test. Design-doc discipline is satisfied rather than violated: the edits fold into the canonical docs (design-editor-packaging.md:141-152, harness-engineering.md:494-504, indexed at docs/design/README.md:164), not a parallel file. The remaining slice (design.mjs staleness, local verify-scenes/verify-tokens build-if-stale, e.g. packages/design-sandbox/scripts/verify-scenes.mjs:65-106) fixes the same root cause in scripts explicitly not on CI, which is at most a minor PR-hygiene preference and non-blocking under this rubric.

verdict.reason: verify-frame.mjs really does rebuild only the shell: buildShellIfStale (lines 82-91) runs `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` and nothing else, main() (line 147) calls only that, and newestSourceMtime (95-108) stats only vite.shell.config.ts, ignoring tsconfig.build.json which drives `build:plugin` (package.json:20). Yet boot() (line 122) starts vite on fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts, which imports `@wafflebase/design-editor` by name (fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17, header comment lines 9-12) and package.json exports "." -> ./dist/plugin/index.js (package.json:6-10); no dist/ is committed. The sibling verify-consumer.mjs already carries the fixed shape (buildIfStale checks dist/shell/index.html AND dist/plugin/index.js and runs `pnpm run build`, lines 203-215; newestSourceMtime stats both configs, 177-179) and its own comment names verify:frame as having the same trap (lines 198-201). I searched for any indirection that would rebuild the plugin before this gate — design-editor package scripts (no pre hook), root package.json scripts, scripts/verify-self.mjs and the lane graph, .github workflows, vite.shell.config.ts outputs (dist/shell only) — and found none; the only other full build is scripts/design.mjs:144, a different entry point. No counterexample exists.

finding.summary: Recent rows for families outside the curated catalog carry no weight, so the preview falls back to wght@400 — the exact failure mode acceptance criteria 2 and 5 call out
finding.evidence: `data-font-weights={entry?.weights}` uses `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY` (the ~105-entry curated catalog). A family picked from the 1,908-entry full library is stored by `addRecentFont` as a bare string (font-recents.ts:53 stores names only) and is absent from the curated index, so `entry` is undefined, the attribute is absent, and `ensurePreviewFontLink` falls through to `previewWeight(undefined)` → `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS.split(';')[0]` → `400`. For a full-library family that ships no 400 cut (`Buda` 300, `UnifrakturCook` 700 — both named in the issue), css2 answers HTTP 400 and the row is stranded in a fallback face. Criterion 5 explicitly requires the weight be derived from what the row renders rather than a curated-catalog lookup that may miss.

verdict.reason: The claimed code shape is not present. `font-family-picker.tsx:243` resolves the recent row's entry as `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY.get(family) ?? fullByFamily?.get(family)`, i.e. it falls back to the full ~1,900-entry index built at :118-124; it is not a curated-catalog-only lookup. The effect at :98-116 loads the full library specifically when a recent is missing from the curated index (`needFullForRecents`), and the full data carries real cuts for the two families the finding names (font-catalog.full.ts:261 Buda weights "300", :1816 UnifrakturCook weights "700"). Additionally, the row is withheld from the preview observer until weights are resolvable: :251 `previewable = entry !== undefined || fullSettled` gates `data-font-row` at :255, and the observer at :138-165 only observes `[data-font-row]` and re-runs on `fullByFamily`/`fullSettled`, so no `wght@400` request can be issued for an unresolved family. A test asserts exactly this: font-family-picker.test.ts:448-479 stores a recent absent from the curated catalog, verifies it is not observed pre-settle (:464), and asserts the preview href contains `:wght@700` and not `wght@400` (:477-478). The only residual default-weight path is a failed dynamic import (fullSettled true, entry undefined), which is an explicit documented fallback (:86-89, :246-250), not the described mechanism, and is a line-level edge rather than a spec/design-fit violation. The finding's criterion-5 paraphrase also conflates ensurePreviewFontLink's docstring about `text` being the row's textContent (font-catalog.ts:253-257) with the weight argument, which is passed per-row from the resolved entry (font-catalog.ts:280).

finding.summary: Canonical design docs still describe the preview path as `ensureFontLink`; the loading-model change is recorded only in the source docstring and in docs/tasks, not folded into the subsystem design docs
finding.evidence: slides-fonts.md:177-184 and :201-202 ("Each visible row previews in its own family via an IntersectionObserver that calls `ensureFontLink` only for on-screen rows") and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:164 ("lazy-loads its CSS via `ensureFontLink(family, weights)` the first time a family is picked, hovered, or previewed") are now factually wrong: previewing goes through the new `ensurePreviewFontLink` with a new DOM contract (`data-wafflebase-font-preview`) and glyph subsetting. Neither doc, nor the `font-catalog.ts` row of the file table (docs-font-controls.md:76), was updated. Nested design docs are not link/ref-checked by CI, so nothing else catches this.

verdict.reason: The canonical subsystem design docs DO record the new preview loading model. docs/design/slides/slides-fonts.md:184-203 has a dedicated bullet for `ensurePreviewFontLink(family, text, weights)` covering the css2 `&text=` glyph subsetting, the single `previewWeight` and its HTTP-400 rationale, the new `data-wafflebase-font-preview` DOM marker explicitly contrasted with `data-wafflebase-font`, the already-loaded-in-full refusal (incl. packages/frontend/index.html's app-shell link), and the unknown-weights hold-back via loadFullFontCatalog(). The reviewer's two quoted sentences are misquotes: slides-fonts.md:220-222 actually reads "an `IntersectionObserver` that calls `ensurePreviewFontLink` only for on-screen rows", and docs-font-controls.md:163-169 continues past the quoted fragment with "*Previewing* a picker row takes the cheaper path — `ensurePreviewFontLink(family, text, weights)` ... See slides-fonts.md for the full loading model." The described API exists at packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:258, so the docs match shipped code. The only residue is the one-line summary-table row docs-font-controls.md:76 still naming only `ensureFontLink`; with accurate prose seven lines below it, that is a minor/nit, not a major design-doc-discipline violation (the required doc is neither missing nor parallel).
